text: Writing clean code is a skill that separates good programmers from great ones. The goal is not just to make the computer understand your instructions, but to make them clear for other humans. First, focus on readable code by using consistent spacing and indentation. Second, follow clear naming conventions: a variable called `customerName` is far better than `x`. Third, break your program into small, focused functions that each do one single job. This makes testing and debugging easier. Ultimately, clean code saves time and money because it is much simpler to maintain and update in the future.
